title: Investigation-first dashboard guides for token serving
content:
Purpose:
This note defines a set of investigation-oriented dashboard patterns and the metric/tracing contracts needed to make fast, accurate incident triage for token-serving workloads. Focus: reduce time-to-root-cause for production latency and quality regressions in inference traffic.

Audience:
- On-call SREs and eng responders
- Runtime engineers working on batching/KV caching
- Dashboard owners and observability SMEs

Summary guidance (one-liner):
Design dashboards for stories, not just signals — each widget should map to a single investigative question with a recommended follow-up action. Capture metric units, typical baselines, and the minimal trace path to validate hypotheses.

Why “investigation-first”?
- Token-serving incidents are often multi-layer: client routing, request coalescing, batching, KV-cache lookups, model kernel stalls.
- Alerts alone cause noisy escalations. Dashboards that presuppose likely root causes reduce chase time.

Investigation stories (example set):
1) Sudden p90/p99 token-latency spike — is it batching, queueing, or slow kernel?
2) P50 stable but downstream error rate rising — is there a model fallback or memory OOM?
3) Regional degradation — routing policy or capacity exhaustion?
4) Increased unit cost per token — smaller batches & more cache misses?

Metric definitions (contract, units, baseline, owner):
- request.count: total inference requests (count), owner: runtime-routing, baseline: depends on route (annotate per-route baseline)
- tokens.generated.total: tokens emitted per request (tokens), owner: runtime-encoder, baseline: median per-route prompt profile
- latency.end_to_end.ms: time from request ingress to response end (ms), owner: runtime, baseline: 30-120 ms for small models, 200-800ms for larger
- latency.decode.ms: model decode time (ms), owner: serving-runtime, baseline: depends on model and seq len
- latency.queue_wait.ms: time request waited before being batched (ms), owner: batching, baseline: 0-20ms for low load; spikes indicate batching backpressure or bursty traffic
- kv_cache.hit_rate.pct: fraction of KV cache hits by token/key (percent), owner: runtime-kv-cache, baseline: high for conversational workloads (>70%)
- batch.size.avg: average tokens per batch (tokens), owner: batching, baseline: model-specific; track distribution percentiles (p50/p90/p99)
- fallback.count: number of requests routed to fallback model (count), owner: routing, baseline: near-zero in steady state
- gpu.utilization.pct: per-GPU utilization (percent), owner: infra, baseline: depends on shard sizing; track per-instance and aggregated
- oom.rate: OOM events per minute (count), owner: runtime, baseline: 0
- error.rate.5m: aggregate request errors (count or percent), owner: runtime, baseline: <0.1%
- cost.per_token.usd: derived unit cost (USD/token), owner: finance+runtime, baseline: tracked per-model and per-deployment

Tracing conventions (span names, attributes, required invariants):
- Top-level trace id is request.trace_id, must propagate through all async queues and batching layers.
- Recommended span naming (short):
  - ingress.router (attrs: route, route_version, customer_id)
  - router.queue_wait (attrs: queue_depth, enqueued_at)
  - router.batch_build (attrs: batch_size_tokens, batch_size_reqs, build_duration_ms)
  - runtime.kv_cache_lookup (attrs: kv_key_count, hit_count, local_hit_pct)
  - runtime.model_infer (attrs: model_name, model_version, seq_len, quantization)
  - runtime.kernel_exec (attrs: kernel_name, exec_ms, gpu_id)
  - response.encode (attrs: tokens_out, bytes_out)
  - fallback.invoke (attrs: fallback_model, reason)
- Span attributes required for triage: model_name, model_version, batch_size_tokens, queue_wait_ms, kv_hit_count, gpu_id, host_region, failure_reason. These must be present or trace considered low-fidelity.
- Trace sampling policy for production inference:
  - 0.5% baseline sampling of full traces (captures typical behavior)
  - 100% sampling for errors (any request with status != 200) and any request with end_to_end latency > configured p99 threshold for that route
  - Rate-limited sampling for high-throughput routes to avoid explosion (max 20 full traces/min per route)
  - If trace includes fallback.invoke, force full-span capture for that trace (helpful for root-cause across model variants)

Dashboard layout patterns (investigation lanes):
- Top row: Incident context cards (current alert summary, affected routes list, recent deploys, baseline SLOs).
- Row A — Overview: request.count (timeseries), end_to_end p50/p90/p99, error.rate.5m. Each card shows short suggested next-step text.
- Row B — Latency decomposition: stacked waterfall or stacked timeseries composed of queue_wait -> decode -> kernel_exec -> response_encode. Show both absolute ms and percent contributions. Add a small table showing top contributors by route.
- Row C — Batching & concurrency: batch.size.avg (timeseries + percentile histogram), queue_depth distribution heatmap, max_batch_wait (99th). Include a small sparkline per shard.
- Row D — KV cache and model variance: kv_cache.hit_rate.pct (heatmap by route+user), fallback.count, model_version split (bar chart showing percent of traffic per version).
- Row E — Traces & cost: sample trace waterfall viewer embed, cost.per_token.usd over time, aggregated tokens.generated.total.
- Bottom row — Investigative quicklinks and runbook: pre-populated filters for traces/logs (slow path, fallback traces, OOM traces), commands for ad-hoc queries.

Concrete widget behavior notes (so dashboard owners implement same interactions):
- For waterfall: clicking a segment (e.g., queue_wait) should filter traces for spans where queue_wait > selected threshold and open trace explorer.
- Heatmaps (kv cache) should allow toggling between per-user and per-route aggregation quickly.
- Model-version bar: clicking a version drills to traces routed to that version and shows recent deploys for that version.

Sampling and cardinality controls (operational):
- Tag cardinality: avoid user_id on high-cardinality timeseries; only allow hashed_user_bucket (10 buckets) for dashboard rollups; raw user_id only in sampled traces/logs.
- High-cardinality attributes allowed only in trace spans and sampled logs; metrics should only contain route, model_name, and region as labels.

Runbook snippets (first 8 actions for paging SRE):
1) Check the Top row cards for affected routes and recent deploys.
2) Filter latency decomposition to last 5 minutes; identify the dominant contributor (queue_wait vs kernel_exec).
3) If queue_wait dominates: check batch.size.avg, queue_depth, and GPU utilization. If GPUs are low utilization and wait is high, suspect routing/queuing misconfiguration.
4) If kernel_exec dominates: check GPU metrics and recent driver/kernel updates; search for oom.rate spikes.
5) If kv_cache hit-rate dropped: pivot to kv cache heatmap; if localized to a user bucket, consider cache poisoning or a prompt-pattern change.
6) Open 3 example traces (links embedded) matching the error/slow criteria; confirm span attributes (batch_size_tokens, model_version, gpu_id).
7) If fallback.count is elevated, identify fallback reason attribute and correlate with deploys or model artifacts.
8) Escalate to runtime-model team with trace ids and top 3 suspect spans if not resolvable in 15 minutes.

Suggested queries and filters (text to copy into trace/log UI):
- slow-requests: trace where latency.end_to_end.ms > {{route.p99.ms}}
- fallback-traces: trace where exists(span.fallback.invoke)
- kv-low-hit: metric kv_cache.hit_rate.pct < 0.5 by route
- oom-traces: trace where span.failure_reason contains "OOM" or metric oom.rate > 0

Acceptance criteria for dashboard changes (PR checklist):
- Every new widget includes: investigative question, baseline, owner, and a single follow-up action.
- All metrics used are in the metric-contracts registry (id/link included).
- Trace links pre-filter to similar traces and include at least one exemplar trace.
- Dashboard rendering must stay under 3s for typical user queries.

Open questions / known gaps:
- We need a standardized short-code for model versions across logs/metrics to avoid freeform strings that break group-by.
- Tracing budget needs to be validated against peak traffic to avoid runaway storage/costs; propose a monthly simulated sampling run.
- We currently do not have per-tenant cost.per_token in high-cardinality form; need to evaluate privacy and cost accuracy tradeoffs.

Next actions (owner assignments):
- Aisha: add metric contracts for queue_wait.ms and batch_build.duration (due 2024-09-05).
- Jonah: implement p99-driven trace sampling rule and validate storage effects (due 2024-10-01).
- Marisol: prototype the investigation lane UI with clickable waterfall (demo at next Observability WG).

Notes to self / scratchpad (keep informal):
- Consider a "trace sparklines" column showing small sample latency distribution per host (fast visual triage).
- For customer-facing incidents, include an obfuscated example trace to explain the root cause in postmortems.

If you iterate on this doc, add small change entries below with date and short note.

-- end --
